full_judgment: 8. Section 72 of the Bangladesh Bank Order, 1972 also grants certain exemptions. The exemption also does not cover. the present decretal amount. According to section 60 of the Code of Civil Procedure the word "property" also includes every type of interest that can be owned by the judgment-debtor over which he possesses power of disposal. Thus, it is seen that "money" is liable to be attached and in the present case money of the judgment-debtor in custody of the Bangladesh Bank kept in the Consolidated Fund is liable to be attached and paid as the same belongs to the Republic of which the judgment-debtor is a department. The decisions cited by Mr. Farooqi in the cases of Muktilal Agarwala Vs. Trustees of the Provident Fund of the Tin Plate Co. of India Ltd and others. AIR 1956 (SC) 336, the case of Smt. Radharani Dass W/o Narayan Chandra Ghose Vs. Smt. Binodamoyee Dassi W/o Abinash Chandra Ghose & others AIR 1942 (Cal) 92 and the case of Shulen Singh and others Vs. Ganendra Kumea Roy Chowdhury, AIR 1950 (Cal) 74 support this view.
